name: claude-pulse
description: Status bar indicator for Claude Code: working, task progress, needs input, done. 100% local — no API calls.

commands.title: Claude Pulse: Show Usage Inside Claude Code

claudePulse.alignment.description: Which side of the status bar the indicator sits on.

claudePulse.priority.description: Position within the chosen side (higher = further left). The default -900 keeps it at the far-right edge, which VS Code preserves when the window is too narrow to show every item.

claudePulse.allProjects.description: Show Claude sessions from every project. Off (default): each window only shows sessions running in its own workspace folders.

claudePulse.doneDisplaySeconds.description: How long the done checkmark stays visible before fading back to idle.

claudePulse.waitingTimeoutSeconds.description: Claude Code fires no event when you APPROVE a permission, so a confirmed permission prompt is shown as working again this many seconds after the last confirmation (repeat notifications re-arm it). Questions and agent prompts are never aged out. 0 disables the timeout.

claudePulse.provisionalWaitSeconds.description: Claude Code fires PermissionRequest for auto-approved calls too, so by default only confirmed prompts (an unanswered dialog, or a question) turn the indicator yellow. If your setup never fires the confirming Notification, set this to e.g. 8 to show unconfirmed permission requests as 'needs input' after that many seconds.

claudePulse.showElapsed.description: Show the elapsed timer while Claude is working.

claudePulse.buddyName.description: Name the buddy calls you in its messages. Empty = auto-detected from git config user.name (first name).

claudePulse.buddyCharacter.description: Which built-in buddy character to show (ignored when buddyImage is set). Bipeds: critter (a red panda), robot. Four-legged: cat, pup, turtle (a tortoise). Slow: turtle, snail. Flyers: bee (small), dragon (big), ghost.

claudePulse.buddyImage.description: Absolute path to your own character image for the Buddy panel (PNG, GIF, WebP, SVG — animated GIFs work). Empty = the built-in character. Easiest via the 'Claude Pulse: Choose Buddy Character' command.

claudePulse.showTokens.description: Append the session's output-token count to the status bar while Claude works.

claudePulse.showLimits.description: Show how much of your 5-hour and weekly Claude limits is left. Read from the usage Claude Code already caches on this machine — no API calls.

claudePulse.limitWarnWeekly.description: Percent of the weekly limit at which the indicator turns amber. It only turns amber if your current pace would also use the rest up before the week refills — a high number with a reset close behind is not worth a warning.

claudePulse.limitWarnSession.description: Percent of the 5-hour limit at which the indicator turns amber. This is the window that usually blocks people mid-work.

claudePulse.contextWarnTokens.description: Flag a conversation once it carries this many tokens. Everything in a conversation is re-read on every reply, so a large one makes each turn cost far more; /compact keeps a summary and drops the rest.

claudePulse.buddyUsageRemarks.description: Let the desktop character mention a usage limit out loud. Turn it off to keep the quiet status bar badge without the commentary.

claudePulse.awayReminder.description: Remind you about fifteen minutes before a large, idle conversation stops being cheap to come back to. Claude keeps a conversation ready for an hour after each reply; after that the next message reloads all of it at full price, and /compact beforehand is the only cheap way round it.

claudePulse.awayWarnTokens.description: How large a conversation has to be before that reminder is worth giving. One reload costs the whole conversation at full price — over ten times an ordinary reply — so this is lower than contextWarnTokens.

claudePulse.keepUsageFresh.description: Have Claude Code fetch a new usage reading once the one it holds is more than twenty minutes old and tokens have been spent since. Left to itself Claude Code refreshes that reading rarely, and every limit warning here starts from it. This runs `claude -p /usage` in the background: Claude Code contacts Anthropic exactly as it does when you type /usage, and it costs no tokens. Where the macOS app is running, the app does this instead.
